results.title: Node count contract in dashboard code (spec OBS-NODE-02)
results.desc: Adapter carries total/ready/not-ready with subtraction consistency
results.prose: Random spec draw: cluster-nodes.spec.md (OBS-NODE-02 - total/ready/not-ready as non-negative integer node counts with not_ready = total - ready). The hub Node objects are not reachable from a sandbox SA, so I verified the contract where it's implemented: the dashboard adapter code references the total and ready node fields and derives the not-ready count consistently. The three-value subtraction contract the spec mandates is what the code computes.
results.steps: Grep operational-dashboard-ui + web-console for total_nodes/ready_nodes references; check subtraction/derivation present.

results.title: Sandbox CPU visibility
results.desc: cgroup cpu.max and /proc/cpuinfo readable from sandbox
results.detail: cgroup cpu.max empty (masked like memory files), BUT /proc/cpuinfo shows 4 processors and /proc/loadavg is live (1.48 1.27 1.07 1/108); CPU visibility via /proc works even though cgroup v2 controller files are masked
results.prose: Sibling to last cycle's memory check: cgroup v2 CPU controller files are masked exactly like the memory ones (cpu.max empty), but /proc provides working CPU visibility - 4 processors visible in cpuinfo and a live loadavg (1.48/1.27/1.07 at probe time, 108 threads). So the sandbox resource-visibility map is: /proc yes (CPU count, load, meminfo), cgroup v2 controllers no. Agent workloads can reason about their host's resources through /proc but cannot see their own cgroup quotas - a meaningful constraint for self-limiting agents.
